newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up on some outage pressure - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up on some outage pressure - Sept 24.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended higher Tuesday, under pressure from rising physicals prices and news of an outage at a California nuclear plant, industry sources said.

Edison International's 1,080 megawatt San Onofre nuclear power unit 3 in San Clemente, Calif. was shut Monday for repairs. The unit was expected to be out of service for two weeks for repairs to the reactor's coolant piping system.
"It definitely had some effect, especially on Palo Verde (PV)," one futures broker said.
Physical electricity prices were also reported to be higher Tuesday with various nuclear and fossil fuel plant outages through the West.
October California Oregon Border (COB) settled up 28 cents at $16.12 after trade as high as $16.25, while November closed steady at $16.70 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Remaining COB deferreds ended steady to up to 30 cents higher.
October PV settled up five cents at $16.48 after trade as low as $16.25, while November PV closed at $15.30 from trade as high as $15.75 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds were steady in thin trade.
NYMEX total estimated volumes were not available, but as of 1400 EDT, COB had traded 268 contracts while PV had traded 88 contracts.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
